subparts.author_derivation: Start with4+x≡A(2−x)+B(1+x). An identity requires the same A,B for every x. At x=2,it yields6=3B; at x=−1,it yields3=3A. These are equations in A or B at a fixed x,not identities in x. They determine A=1,B=2; substituting these back restores an identity. The printed key states the all-values versus particular-value distinction and notes equating constant terms corresponds to x=0.
